newsitem.title: USA: Sallie Mae shareholder group protests suit.
newsitem.headline: Sallie Mae shareholder group protests suit.

text.p: An opposition shareholder group voiced its objections on Monday to a lawsuit the Student Loan Marketing Association (Sallie Mae) filed regarding a special shareholder meeting.

Sallie Mae management and the shareholder group, the Committee to Restore Value at Sallie Mae (CRV) are fighting over proposals on how to change Sallie Mae from a government-sponsored enterprise to a private corporation.

Sallie Mae filed suit against the shareholder group on Friday. The attorney representing management said the group, which has called a special shareholder meeting for May 9, sent materials to shareholders that did not go through the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission registration process.
The Sallie Mae suit seeks a temporary restraining order and a preliminary injunction until "corrective disclosure" is made, clarifying the date and nature of the group's meeting.
Sallie Mae management has scheduled its own meeting for May 15 at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT and the special meeting sought by the shareholder group four hours later the same day.
The opposition group, headed by Albert Lord, a Sallie Mae director, has said it believes it has the right to schedule its meeting whenever it wants.
"By filing this suit, Sallie Mae's management has again said it will listen to its shareholders only if a court orders it to," Lord said on Monday.

Richard Brusca, an attorney with Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher and Flom LLP, representing management, said on April 18: "We believe the CRV needs to file its materials and have it subject to the same review as our materials."
